newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market steady at $70 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market steady at $70 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold in light to moderate activity at $70.00 per cwt, unchanged from sales earlier this week, but down $1.00 from a week ago, feedlot sources said.
About 5,000 head sold in Kansas, with no sales reported in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, they said.
The sales in Kansas may have been off next week's showlists, some sources said, as much of this week's showlists in Kansas and the Panhandle were depleted.
Next week's showlists were expected to be steady to slightly below this week, they said.
The showlists also were expected to hold a large number of short-fed cattle as owners continue to market them early while they are still making money, the sources said.
AT $70.00, cattle owners reportedly were earning $85.00 per head, according to a Kansas feedlot operator said.

Beef demand this week was said to be strong, although prices were pressured by large slaughter, sources said. Thursday's slaughter was estimated by USDA at 133,000 head, which brought the week-to-date figure to 512,000, USDA said. The number was up 7.6 percent from a week ago, but down 1.8 percent from a year ago.
